abstract: Yang et al. show that C. elegans embryos adapt to tetraploidy and maintain viability by scaling their transcriptome proportionately to their increased cell volume. Tetraploids display slower cell cycles and prolonged embryogenesis due to an elevated DNA-cell volume ratio.
